events.title: The death of Pope St. Gregory VII in exile
events.shortBlurb: The reforming pope of the Investiture Controversy, who brought the emperor to penance at Canossa, died in exile at Salerno…
body: On 25 May 1085 Pope St. Gregory VII, the monk Hildebrand, died at Salerno, an exile from his own city. He had been the leading spirit of the reform that bears his name, striving to free the Church from lay control, to end the buying and selling of offices, and to enforce clerical discipline.

His long struggle with the Emperor Henry IV over the right to invest bishops brought the emperor to penance in the snow at Canossa, but ended with Gregory driven from Rome by imperial arms. His last words are remembered: “I have loved justice and hated iniquity, therefore I die in exile.” He was canonized in 1606.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 25 May
